book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Discrimination against old false images

indicators.note: false pictures are not true ones, so the letters of images are recast into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Prejudice against the elderly rests on misleading pictures of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice on grounds of a person's age, most often aimed at older people.

clue.text: I'd look after the last king (Commonwealth's first king): can't get out of it

definitions.note: a description of a jam, standing for the noun

indicators.note: I'd look comes after the last king, so the words for those two are placed behind the royal cipher

parts.note: George VI was Britain's last king, and GR (Georgius Rex) is his royal cipher
taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: the first of Commonwealth means only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A loyal servant pledging to tend the last monarch, with a puzzling aside about the Commonwealth's first king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like 'look after', meaning care for, but it is the order signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridlock is traffic jammed so solidly that no vehicle can move, a situation nobody can escape.

clue.text: Everyone in religious musical is brought up to be soothing

indicators.note: everyone sits in religious, so the word for everyone goes inside the short word for pious

parts.note: pi is a colloquial short form of pious
all people

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: Children raised on a devotional stage show are supposed to grow up calm and calming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious musical' reads as one phrase, like Godspell, but it splits: religious gives PI and the musical is Evita.
explanation.definitionFit: A palliative relieves symptoms or eases pain without curing, so it is soothing in effect.

clue.text: All beer to drunk is passable

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and disordered, so these words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Any beer at all is fine for someone who has already had a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means acceptable without being good, the same middling grade as passable.

clue.text: Taser's second barrel

definitions.note: used here as a verb: to shock with an electric weapon

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: Someone describes a stun gun, saying its second part is the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To Taser someone is to disable them with an electric shock, which is to stun them.

clue.text: Letter from Elia — prosecutor

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
a DA is a US district attorney, a public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A prosecutor receives a letter from someone called Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet, corresponding to L.

clue.text: Determined to begin circumventing asinine law

indicators.note: to circumvent is literally to go around, so start goes around the other letters

parts.note: to start

indicators.note: an asinine thing is foolish and muddled, so the letters of law are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A resolute campaigner sets out to find a way round a stupid law.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart supporter is steadfast and resolute, firmly committed to a cause.

clue.text: Girl's right and Gable made her love him

indicators.note: 's stands for has: the girl has, holds, right inside her

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl's view of Clark Gable, who made her fall for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Judy Garland sang 'Dear Mr Gable (You Made Me Love You)' to Clark Gable in Broadway Melody of 1938.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer and actress famously serenaded the film star with a song about loving him, so the line identifies her.

clue.text: 50% of false teeth are hollow

indicators.note: half of the eight letters are kept, so only the first four survive

parts.note: a set of false teeth is a denture

explanation.surface: A dentist's claim that half of all false teeth are hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface.

clue.text: He's ostracized in Mormon state bordered by broken coast

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun: one who is ostracized

indicators.note: the state's letters have the other letters running along either side of them
a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of coast are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Utah, home of the Mormon church, is abbreviated UT

explanation.surface: A man shunned in Utah, a state hemmed in by a ruined shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: Utah is landlocked, so the 'broken coast' is pure invention for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected and shut out by society.

clue.text: Disinclination to do anything effectual for lip dimension for a second

indicators.note: the second for in the clue: dimension for a second means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: lip is cheek or impudence, which is insolence
S is the abbreviation for second
D is the abbreviation for dimension, as in 3-D

explanation.surface: A lazy person's reluctance to act is put down to lip, measured in seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Lip in the sense of cheeky talk gives INSOLENCE, and D for dimension replaces its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolence is habitual laziness, an unwillingness to exert oneself or do anything useful.

clue.text: Very wealthy man, the Spanish prize funder

parts.note: a nob is a rich or upper-class person
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A rich Spaniard bankrolls an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel left his fortune to endow the prizes that carry his name.

clue.text: Money (low note)

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry: money, with a bracketed gloss about a deep musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' suggests a deep note, but here it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is an informal slang synonym for cash, of American origin.

clue.text: Future president swaps Ohio for a city state

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means taking it out and putting the other in its place
pairs what goes out with what comes in

parts.note: Barack Obama, a future president when the clue was set
O is a traditional abbreviation for Ohio
taken as written
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A rising politician trades one state for a city state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City state' reads as one phrase like Singapore, but 'city' gives LA and 'state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the US states in the Deep South.

clue.text: Hard type of man, worker in Eden originally

parts.note: Adam, the first man, is the type or pattern of all men
a worker ant
taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of Eden is used

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A tough fellow labouring in the Garden of Eden at the beginning of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine means unbreakably hard, like the legendary adamant stone.

clue.text: Working up to steal claim

indicators.note: working dough or clay kneads it into a new shape, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone building up to a theft lays claim to the goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working up to' reads as an idiom meaning preparing for, but 'Working' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To postulate is to assert or assume something as true, which is to claim it.

clue.text: Arnold's offer to IKEA via letter that goes astray

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander from their places, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Arnold makes the furniture store a proposal in a letter that gets lost in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arnold's offer' frames the phrase as one man's final terms; the definition is the offer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying take it or leave it presents a final, non-negotiable offer.

clue.text: Sheriff's officer gives helpful advice to officers who help

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint
staff officers assist a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A sheriff's deputy offers useful pointers to the officers who assist him.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer, in Scotland an officer serving a sheriff, named for his metal-tipped staff.

clue.text: Drive out demons with energy. Cross and crozier almost disintegrated

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: something disintegrated has broken apart, so the letters are reassembled
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of crozier is dropped

parts.note: a bishop's hooked staff

explanation.surface: A priest attacks evil spirits with vigour, his cross and crozier falling to pieces in the struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Z spelling comes straight from crozier, so the answer takes the -ize form.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcize is to expel evil spirits from a person or place by ritual.

clue.text: Impressive quality of Portugal or Spanish wine

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
taken as written
tent is a deep red wine from Spain, used as communion wine

explanation.surface: A wine buff weighs the grandeur of Portuguese against Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portugal or' suggests port, but Portugal gives only P.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides an omen, a portent is a marvel, and Chambers allows it the sense of impressiveness or momentousness.

clue.text: Comment on Evangelist

parts.note: re means on or concerning
Mark is one of the four Gospel writers

explanation.surface: A note commenting on one of the Gospel writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a brief spoken or written observation.

clue.text: Anonymous gipsy men's peculiar charm

parts.note: the Roma are the Romani people

explanation.surface: Unnamed travelling men have an odd fascination about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition, in its sense of distinctive.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma can be a subtle, distinctive quality or atmosphere surrounding something.

clue.text: Sailor told to go away

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman
someone told to go is sent away

explanation.surface: A seaman is ordered to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go away' reads as the order, but 'away' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, the sense of away in 'she is away today'.

clue.text: Psalmist forgetting God in the grip of desire

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms
D is short for Deus, Latin for God, as in D.V. (Deo volente)

explanation.surface: The Psalmist, overcome by longing, loses sight of God.
explanation.walkthrough: David's lapse with Bathsheba gives the surface its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or greedy, consumed by a strong wish for something.

clue.text: Was secretary heard to entice?

indicators.note: the clue's sense is caught by ear, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: to temp is to work as a temporary secretary

explanation.surface: Did a secretary's flirting get noticed by the office?
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt is to lure or attract someone towards something.

clue.text: Scottish island with no independent ancestral line

indicators.note: having no means the letter for independent is taken out

parts.note: Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A Hebridean island lacks any independent line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree charts a person's ancestors and descendants.

clue.text: Book adapted for TV is one clue

indicators.note: an adaptation reshapes material, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novel reworked for television turns out to be a single clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book adapted for TV' reads as a dramatization; the definition is just 'Book', one of the Bible's.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviticus is the third book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Would you say bearskin signified agitation?

indicators.note: asking how something would be said points to a sound-alike

parts.note: a bear's skin is fur, and signified is meant

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a guardsman's fur hat stood for unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: A bearskin is also the tall fur hat of Britain's Guards regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferment is a state of unrest or excitement.

clue.text: Inhabitant's end varied with current form of Buddhism

indicators.note: varied means altered, so the letters of end are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current
Zen is the meditative school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A resident's life ends with a change of current into a Buddhist practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A denizen is a resident or occupant of a place.
